html:
The Kharijites were an early Muslim movement that broke with the caliph Ali after the Battle of Siffin in 657. Their name means "those who went out".

They objected to Ali's agreeing to arbitration with Muawiya, arguing that judgement belongs to God alone. They held that any Muslim who committed a major sin was no longer a believer and could be fought, and that the caliph should be the best Muslim, whatever his tribe. Ali defeated them at Nahrawan in 658, but a Kharijite assassin killed him in 661 in the mosque at Kufa.

They rose repeatedly against the Umayyads. Their later heirs, the Ibadis, survive today in Oman and parts of North Africa.
